title: `torch.Tensor.aminmax` crash with `INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED` when input's shape contains 0

labels.name: module: cuda
labels.description: Related to torch.cuda, and CUDA support in general

labels.name: module: error checking
labels.description: Bugs related to incorrect/lacking error checking

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: This issue has been looked at a team member, and triaged and prioritized into an appropriate module

body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug When `torch.Tensor.aminmax` recieves an empty input tensor on cuda, it will crash with `INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED`. However, the same code can run well on CPU device and return: ``` torch.return_types.aminmax( min=tensor([]), max=tensor([])) ``` This unexpected behavior occurs on PyTorch 1.11.0\1.12.0\1.13.0\1.13.1, and even in the nightly version(2.0.0.dev20230219). It should be related to [#85439](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/85439) ### To Reproduce ```python import torch def test(input): return torch.Tensor.aminmax(input,dim=0) # device = "cpu" device = "cuda" input = torch.ones([10, 0], dtype=torch.float32) x=test(input.to(device)) print(x) ``` The error result is ``` Traceback (most recent call last): File "test.py", line 9, in x=test(input.to(device)) File "test.py", line 4, in test return torch.Tensor.aminmax(input,dim=0) RuntimeError: iter.numel() > 0 && iter.ntensors() - iter.noutputs() == 1 && iter.noutputs() >= 1 INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED at "/opt/conda/conda-bld/pytorch_1670525552843/work/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Reduce.cuh":1134, please report a bug to PyTorch. ``` ### Expected behavior I hope this function could maintain consistent behavior on CPU and Cuda (e.g., fix crash behavior on Cuda). ### Versions
